title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Louisville Village Board of Trustees met Thursday evening and moved quickly through a light agenda.

Mayor Chris Rinehart called the meeting to order. With no visitors asking to speak, the board approved the meeting agenda, past meeting minutes and the bills.

Mayor Rinehart then opened the floor for public comment and called on Damon Simmons, owner of DBS Disposal, Louisville’s trash vendor. Simmons introduced Louisville resident Steve Stortzum as the proposed new owner who will take over the company August 3. The men said there will be no change in operations. Simmons will stay on for an undetermined time to help with a smooth transition. Stortzum said the business will operate out of Louisville rather than Farina, bringing another business to town.  Simmons asked trustees to approve a contract revision that adds Stortzum as the owner as Simmons works toward retirement. Village Attorney Kyle Boose noted the current contract expires June 30, 2028. The board approved the revised contract with no objections.

Engineer Brandon Bridges of Charleston Engineering in Olney presented the annual oil and chip contract for local streets. Bridges said the lone bidder, Larry Heuerman Trucking of Teutopolis, submitted a bid of $37,912. The company will perform the work sometime after mid-July. The board approved the contract.

Mayor Rinehart asked the board to honor North Clay High School student Briley Mullens, a newly selected state officer for FCCLA. He suggested placing signs recognizing her accomplishment at the north and south entrances to Louisville. Following the precedent of earlier honorees, the village will buy the signs from Meagher Sign and Graphic in Flora for $590. The board approved the purchase unanimously.

Rinehart also updated the board on plans for new Welcome to Louisville signage at the four entrances to the village. He said he is discussing placement with several parties, including Ameren. He asked trustees to help decide the look of the signs, what information they should include, and whether the village should place signs on Route 45 and additionally at the east and west entrances. No decisions were made, but the project is moving forward.

During open time trustees touched on several topics but took no action. They revisited the previously approved privacy fencing near the water storage tank and the adjoining property owned by Nancy Byers. Utilities Superintendent Troy Elwood said the fence will be 90 feet long. After Byers questioned its fence placement, Elwood said the village will use GIS measurements. Byers also requested trees in that area. Both Elwood and the mayor said that would not be a problem.

Trustee Tim Davis raised concerns about the tornado siren. He noted that no siren sounded during recent severe storms that caused damage in the area. Rinehart said the siren does work, but someone must trigger it manually. A suggestion arose to contact Clay County ESDA about activating the siren remotely. Davis also said the K-1 building, which serves as the tornado shelter, needs to be open during storms. The mayor said he retrieved the key recently and opened the shelter when needed, but noted a better solution is needed.  Supt. Elwood said he will talk with Security Alarm, the company that provides the village’s security cameras. He suggested installing a magnetic lock that the village can trigger remotely. He said the same solution could also make it easier to open the public bathrooms at the new pavilion when it is in use as well as other times.

The board continued its discussion on how best to handle nuisance properties in the village, but no action was taken.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S ACCIDENT
full_story:
On Wednesday, at approximately 2:38 pm an off-duty deputy and K-9 Chief were involved in a motor vehicle crash.

The two were returning home from training and were traveling south on CR-1 (Big Four Rd) following a box truck.  As the deputy approached 2100 N, a semi-tractor trailer traveling north came across the center of the road striking the box truck.  The deputy took evasive action and swerved off the west side of the road, down an embankment and came to rest in the ditch to avoid being struck by the semi-tractor trailer.  The deputy and K-9 Chief were uninjured.

The deputy immediately began to render aid and requested EMS.  The crash is being investigated by the Illinois State Police.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: MURDER CHARGES
full_story:
The Richland County State’s Attorney’s Office Thursday charged 25-year-old Dylan Jones with six counts of First Degree Murder.  He is facing 4 counts of Murder/Intent to Kill/Injure and 2 counts of Murder/Strong Probability Kill/Injure.

The initial investigation indicates Dylan Jones struck John Jones Jr in the head with a sharp-edged instrument and stabbed Deborah Jones with a knife.  The coroner is conducting medical examinations to determine official causes of death.  Officers found John Jones and Deborah Jones in their individual houses Tuesday afternoon.

Jones will be held in custody until an evaluation to determine his fitness is completed.  His next scheduled court appearance will be on July 23rd.

title: BREAKFAST BITES & BUSINESS INSIGHTS
full_story:

title: GAS UTILITY CONSTRUCTION BOOTCAMP
full_story:
Wabash Valley College will host a new Gas Utility Construction Bootcamp, a hands-on training program designed to prepare students for entry-level careers in the natural gas utility and pipeline construction industry.  The bootcamp runs Monday, August 3rd through 14th.

The intensive 2-week course will be held from 8 am to 6 pm at the WVC campus in Mt. Carmel, offering 90 hours of expert training in gas main and service installation, safety protocols, and readiness for Department of Transportation Operator Qualifications (OQ).

Class size is limited to 10 students.  The full bootcamp investment is $1,200, which includes industry-recognized certifications and job placement support.

Applicants must attend all sessions, pass a background check and drug screening, maintain a clean driving record, and be willing to travel or relocate for job opportunities.

People who want to apply for the program can visit https://iecc.edu/gas-utility.

title: USDA ACCEPTS 2.2 MILLION ACRES
full_story:
Out of 2.5 million acres submitted by farmers and landowners for USDA’s 2026 Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), the department accepted 2.2 million acres.

Through CRP, USDA’s Farm Service Agency offers agricultural producers and landowners incentive payments for their conservation efforts while benefiting their agricultural operations and protecting the nation’s natural resources.

Nearly 2.5 million acres were submitted through the General, Grassland and Continuous CRP signups.  Because the program’s total acreage is capped at 27 million acres for fiscal year 2026, only 2.2 million acres were available for enrollment, making for a highly competitive process for those who submitted offers for CRP.

Of the nearly 1.5 million acres set to expire on September 30th, producers submitted re-enrollment offers for just over 982,000 acres.  Additionally, producers submitted offers to enroll 1.5 million acres of new land.

Nebraska, Colorado and South Dakota hold the top three slots for accepted acres for all 2026 CRP enrollment opportunities.

title: IFB ANNUAL MEETING CHANGES
full_story:
The Illinois Farm Bureau’s Annual Meeting schedule includes some lineup changes and will be a week later than in past years.

This year’s event, with the theme “Farming for the Next Generation,” will be December 12th through 15th at the Hyatt Regency in Chicago.

One lineup change is IFB President Philip Nelson will give his address Sunday morning rather than Saturday night.  Also, in lieu of a concert Saturday night, a keynote speaker will take the stage.

“We’re looking forward to being back at the Hyatt Regency Chicago for the 2026 IFB Annual Meeting.  Building on the success of last year’s event, we’re excited to welcome a keynote speaker back to the program and create an even better experience for attendees,” Donna Gallivan, IFB conference and program manager, told FarmWeek.

Some of the awards typically presented during Sunday morning’s general session, at which Nelson will speak, also will move to Saturday night.  The county awards will continue to be Sunday morning, along with the Young Leader program, which is held before the general session.

The Saturday night member appreciation reception also will include live music this year.  Attendees can look forward to other popular events, including Discussion Meet, IAA Foundation auction and ice cream social, micro talks and the exhibit hall.

The health fair, which has been a growing piece of the exhibit hall, could include more participants and testing for members, Gallivan said, adding she has received numerous inquiries from potential participants.  In past years, attendees could get their blood pressure taken, get screened for skin and prostate cancer and glaucoma, as well as other health screenings.

IFB’s premier event moved from the Palmer House to the Hyatt Regency last year as the hotel offers a larger space.  Registration has hovered around 1,700 since 2024.

The later date this year is because hotels in the Chicago area are booked for an event during the typical timeframe in early December.

More details, including the keynote speaker, micro talk topics and possible additions to the schedule, will be announced at a later date.

Registration will run October 1st to November 13th, and members can register with their county Farm Bureaus.

title: PROTECTING THE MOST VULNERABLE
full_story:
The Better Business Bureau is highlighting the importance of families and caregivers watching out for scams impacting those suffering from Alzheimer’s disease.

According to the BBB, most scams involve complex mental tasks that often target the most vulnerable, like those living with Alzheimer’s.

Don O’Brien, a scam investigator, has this message for those families and caregivers.

O’Brien says one of the best ways to avoid scams: if something feels off, tell someone you trust.

title: OLNEY MURDER ARREST
full_story:
Dylan M. Jones, 25 of Olney was jailed in connection with a double homicide Tuesday.  Jones was booked into the Richland County jail Tuesday night at 11:34 pm.

The dead were identified as John D. Jones, Jr, 52 and Deborah J. Jones, 73 of Olney.  Officers responded to two homes in the 400 block of East Monroe Street in Olney at 3:11 pm Tuesday afternoon and found the victims in their separate houses.
